rows: Offered by LNIPE, several state universities (Punjabi University Patiala, Guru Nanak Dev University Amritsar), and a growing number of private universities (Manipal, Amity, Chandigarh University, and others). Curriculum quality and lab access vary far more by specific college than the degree name suggests, check for an actual biomechanics lab, GPS/wearable tech, and internship tie-ups with a sports team or federation before enrolling.
LNIPE (Lakshmibai National Institute of Physical Education)
B.P.E.S/B.P.Ed 3-4 years; M.P.Ed and MSc specializations 2 years

India's premier government institute for physical education and sports science, with its main campus in Gwalior and regional centres. Admission runs through the LNIPE Entrance Exam plus a physical fitness test, and seats are limited nationally, making this a genuinely competitive route, not a fallback option.
NIS Patiala (Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sports)
Diploma in Sports Coaching, roughly 10 months per discipline

Run under the Sports Authority of India, this is the country's most respected coaching-specific credential, offered discipline by discipline (athletics, cricket, hockey, and more). Seats per discipline are very small, and admission has historically favoured players of national standing or candidates recommended by a national sports federation, this is the single most competitive entry point in this entire field.
Weeks to a few months of study, plus an exam

The NSCA's Certified Strength and Conditioning Specialist (CSCS) is the credential most Indian sports teams and serious academies actually look for in a strength coach, and it requires a bachelor's degree as a requirement. ACSM certifications carry similar weight for exercise-physiology-leaning roles. ISSA and NASM personal-training certifications have a far lower bar and are common among gym-floor trainers rather than team-level S&C coaches.
